name: GATE-CSD
title: CSD registration active at closing
checklist_text: CSD registration active with current banking, director and address details; correct report type (FULL vs summary) printed within this buyer's freshness window (7 days to 3 months - read the pack)
guidance: Appears in essentially every full pack. Several buyers disqualify at evaluation if you are not registered at closing time. Some buyers reject the summary report and demand the FULL registration report; at least one asks for the summary - read each pack. Incorrect or outdated information may itself be a cause for disqualification.
evidence_required: CSD registration report (full or summary per pack), printed inside the buyer's freshness window

name: GATE-TCS
title: SARS Tax Compliance Status PIN current
checklist_text: SARS TCS PIN current - generated for this bid; one PIN per JV partner AND per subcontractor where applicable
guidance: In every pack with bid conditions. Keep eFiling in order year-round. Some buyers invalidate at closing, most verify at award with a 7-working-day cure window; several buyers demand an ORIGINAL tax clearance certificate (often via an MBD 2 returnable), rejecting certified copies - a recurring older-template trait, not a one-off.
evidence_required: Current TCS PIN (per JV partner / subcontractor)

name: GATE-DEFAULTERS
title: Not listed on the Register for Tender Defaulters / Restricted Suppliers
checklist_text: Entity AND every director, member, shareholder and trustee checked against National Treasury's Register for Tender Defaulters and List of Restricted Suppliers
guidance: Automatic, no-cure disqualification with near-identical wording across packs. Check before committing bid costs.
evidence_required: Documented check of National Treasury's lists for the entity and every director

name: GATE-STATE-EMP
title: No director in the service of the state
checklist_text: No director in the service of the state - or the executive-authority approval letter for outside remunerative work attached
guidance: About half of packs bar bids from state employees and companies with state-employed directors outright. Where a director is a state employee, one pack accepts the approval-letter route.
evidence_required: SBD/MBD 4 disclosure; executive-authority approval letter where applicable

name: GATE-CIPC
title: CIPC documents certified and fresh, with signing authority
checklist_text: CIPC registration certificate, director IDs, share certificates and board resolution naming the authorised signatory - certified by a Commissioner of Oaths within the last 90 days, from originals (no copies of certified copies)
guidance: The explicit under-3-months rejection rule is a municipal/checklist-buyer trait, and several of those buyers also reject copies of certified copies entirely - the standing 90-day re-certification cycle keeps you safe everywhere.
evidence_required: Certified CIPC set + signing resolution, certification under 90 days old

name: GATE-BBBEE
title: B-BBEE evidence current (soft gate - points only)
checklist_text: B-BBEE evidence current: SANAS-accredited certificate (large enterprises) or sworn EME/QSE affidavit on the DTIC template (valid 12 months) - CHECK WHICH TABLE the certificate sits in: in the great majority of packs missing it only costs preference points (STILL SUBMIT), but where it sits in a pass/fail pre-qualification or administrative-compliance table it is a hard gate (see GATE-BBBEE-PREQUAL)
guidance: In the great majority of packs, missing B-BBEE evidence scores 0 preference points but does not render the bid non-responsive - if it is not ready at deadline and B-BBEE is NOT a pre-qualification gate in this pack, still submit the bid. Exception: where the pack lists the B-BBEE certificate/level inside a pass/fail pre-qualification or administrative-compliance table (Eskom cl. 3.17-style; TASEZ demands a minimum Level 3), missing or expired proof disqualifies outright - GATE-BBBEE-PREQUAL covers that case. Also: some specific-goals tables award zero points for B-BBEE at all - read the buyer's table. In a close 80/20 race zero points is usually fatal to winning, so keep it current.
evidence_required: B-BBEE certificate or EME/QSE sworn affidavit

name: GATE-BBBEE-PREQUAL
title: B-BBEE as a pass/fail pre-qualification gate (PPPFA pre-qual packs)
checklist_text: Where the pack lists the B-BBEE certificate/level inside a pass/fail pre-qualification or administrative-compliance table: valid proof of the demanded minimum level IN THE BID AT CLOSING - missing or expired proof disqualifies outright; the 'still submit without B-BBEE' rule does NOT apply here
guidance: Corpus-verified exception to the B-BBEE soft-gate rule: Eskom Standard Conditions cl. 3.17-style packs disqualify at closing where B-BBEE level is a pre-qualification criterion; TASEZ demands a minimum Level 3 in its pass/fail Stage-1 administrative table. v3: auto-applies as a CHECK task via deterministic buyer match on the bid's institution (patterns in trigger_condition - fixture data, desk-editable) for buyers whose packs have carried pass/fail B-BBEE tables. Caveat from the 2026-08 buyer sheets: all 10 sampled Eskom packs treated B-BBEE as preference-points-only, so the row is a per-pack verification (which table does the certificate sit in?), not proof of a gate. For any other buyer, add the rule to the checklist manually when triage finds B-BBEE inside a pass/fail table.
evidence_required: Valid B-BBEE certificate/affidavit at the demanded minimum level, in the bid at closing

name: GATE-SUBCONTRACT
title: Subcontracting stance checked before structuring the bid
checklist_text: Subcontracting stance checked: banned, consent-gated (GCC default: no subcontracting without prior written consent), capped (the preference-points-linked cap reads 25% OR 30% depending on the pack - read the number), or mandatory (30% regimes with shortfall penalties, biting from as low as R4m; CIDB CSDG/CPG gazetted goals auto-trigger and can be small, e.g. 5%) - bid structured accordingly, every intended subcontractor disclosed with its own compliance pack (CSD, TCS PIN, B-BBEE, CIPC, CIDB where relevant)
guidance: Subcontracting rules appear in most packs and cut in every direction - four stances: banned outright at some buyers, consent-gated by default elsewhere (GCC boilerplate), capped at 25-30% elsewhere, mandatory 30% to designated enterprises at others - with financial penalties for shortfall (one SOE penalises undisclosed subcontracting at up to 10% of contract value). 100% pass-through is also banned at some buyers - you cannot subcontract the whole works. Non-disclosure of an intended subcontractor is treated as a false declaration. Mandatory-quota relief mechanisms exist (Engineer-approved motivated application).
evidence_required: SBD/MBD 4 subcontractor disclosure + per-subcontractor compliance pack

name: GATE-COIDA
title: COIDA Letter of Good Standing (works / site-based services)
trigger_condition: {"any_of": [{"regime_matches": ["cidb"]}, {"subject_matches": ["construction", "bridge", "civil works", "building works", "roadworks", "road works", "fencing", "guarding", "security service", "security solution", "cleaning service", "landscaping"]}]}
checklist_text: COIDA Letter of Good Standing current (Compensation Fund) - some buyers verify it ONLINE on evaluation day, so 'valid at submission' is not enough; no-employee bidders keep a commissioned exemption affidavit ready
guidance: Concentrated in works and site-based services. Bid-stage disqualifier at some buyers, contract-signing condition at others. Wave-1 (findings F-04): the CIDB regime is now a TRIGGER rather than a fence - the rule still fires on every CIDB bid exactly as before, and ALSO via deterministic subject-matter match on works and site-based-services tenders run under other regimes: RNM 8/2/RNM0614 (bridge construction run under MBD) demanded a Letter of Good Standing with the Workmen's Compensation Commissioner as returnable A2, and VCW403/SECURE/25 (SBD security services) listed a certified COIDA Letter of Good Standing among its immediate-disqualification pre-qualifiers. Patterns are fixture data.
evidence_required: COIDA Letter of Good Standing (or commissioned no-employee exemption affidavit)

name: GATE-RATES
title: Municipal rates clearance - company AND every director
checklist_text: Municipal rates and taxes clearance for the COMPANY and EVERY DIRECTOR - the arrears threshold is BUYER-SPECIFIC (90 days at some, ONE month at others, including arrears with any other municipality) and a settlement arrangement can save you; renters use a certified lease (plus affidavit at some buyers); start collecting director proofs on day one
guidance: The signature municipal-regime gate (all municipal packs, plus TVET colleges and municipal entities). The arrears threshold runs 1-3 months by buyer (Kokstad 90 days per director, Kouga one month including other municipalities' arrears), and some buyers demand the clearance only from the recommended bidder rather than every bidder at submission - check the certificate's own wording and when it bites. v3: per-buyer arrears windows from the 2026-08 buyer sheets ship as data in params.arrears_windows (Tshwane 90 days incl. every director; Cape Town >3 months to ANY municipality plus a payment-deduction authorisation returnable; Mogale no-arrears-at-closing; eThekwini AOD-by-closing with no fixed window). This is the most commonly fatal municipal document and takes days to collect. Wave-1 (findings F-04): the MBD regime is now a TRIGGER rather than a fence - the rule still fires on every MBD bid exactly as before, and ALSO on water-board buyers outside the municipal regime: Vaal Central Water (an SBD-regime PFMA water board) made an original/certified municipal rates clearance certificate not older than 3 months an immediate-disqualification pre-qualifier on VCW403/SECURE/25. Regime and value are priors, not fences.
evidence_required: Rates clearance / statements for company and every director, or certified lease + affidavit
params: {"arrears_windows": [{"match": "tshwane", "detail": "90 days / 3 months; account statement not older than 3 months; applies to the entity AND every owner/member/director/major shareholder individually"}, {"match": "cape town", "detail": "More than 3 months in arrears (SCM Reg 38(1)(d)(i)) - entity or any director, owed to CCT or ANY other municipality; Schedule F.8 pre-authorises the City to deduct arrears from contract payments"}, {"match": "mogale", "detail": "Account not older than 90 days and NOT in arrears at closing; entity + every director; granular substitute-document ladder (lease, councillor/tribal-authority letter, sworn affidavits for spousal/trust/indigent cases)"}, {"match": "ethekwini", "detail": "No fixed day window - arrears blocks award unless an Acknowledgement of Debt was in place AT TENDER CLOSING; applies to commitments to ANY municipality; failing to state account numbers or sign the Declaration of Municipal Fees is itself fatal"}, {"match": "kouga", "detail": "One month, including arrears with any other municipality"}]}

name: GATE-CIDB
title: CIDB grading - exact class, ACTIVE at close and through validity
checklist_text: CIDB grading at the exact class and designation demanded, ACTIVE and in good standing at close AND throughout the validity period - but CHECK THE ELIGIBILITY CLAUSE for a registration grace period before self-eliminating: some buyers accept bidders capable of being registered within 21 WORKING DAYS of closing (proof of application at closing, registration by award); JV: combined grading per CIDB rules, lead partner within one grade, SIGNED JV agreement before submission (notarised formation document + all-partner power of attorney where the pack demands it)
guidance: An absolute eligibility gate where present: 'AN INACTIVE OR SUSPENDED REGISTRATION STATUS WILL INVALIDATE THE TENDER' - keep that zero-tolerance reading as the default. Corpus-verified exception: some buyers (Eskom, Joe Gqabi DM) accept bidders 'capable of being so registered within twenty-one (21) working days from the closing date' - proof of application suffices at closing, registration due by award, and this CIDB cure clock can exceed the pack's general cure window. Read the eligibility clause before self-eliminating. A letter of intent to formalise a JV later is expressly rejected; at some buyers a signed-but-unnotarised JV agreement fails eligibility - book the notary early. Wave-1 (findings F-04): the CIDB regime is now a TRIGGER rather than a fence - the rule still fires on every CIDB bid exactly as before, and ALSO via deterministic subject-matter match on construction-works tenders run under other regimes: RNM 8/2/RNM0614 (Construction of Mgodlwa Bridge, run under MBD) made a 6CE-or-higher CIDB grading its first eligibility gate, and VCW403/SECURE/25's Section 2 (perimeter security fencing and related works) demanded 4 SQ PE or higher under SBD. Patterns are fixture data.
evidence_required: CIDB registration at the demanded grade; signed (and where demanded notarised) JV agreement

name: GATE-SECTOR
title: Sector statutory registrations (PSIRA / NHBRC / professional councils / OEM)
checklist_text: Sector registrations valid, active, correct class/grade for the entity AND named individuals: PSIRA (security), NHBRC (housing), ECSA/SACQSP/SACPCMP (built environment), LPC + Fidelity Fund (legal), HPCSA/SANC (health), Banks Act, waste licences, OEM authorisations (ICT)
guidance: Always pass/fail where they appear. Proof must be certified, current, and match the exact grade/class demanded - often for named individuals, not just the firm. v3: auto-applies via deterministic buyer match for buyers whose packs carry named accreditation gates - Department of Tourism demands a valid SETA/QCTO accreditation letter for the advertised qualification (failure to submit disqualifies, and the demanded SETA changes per bid). Wave-1 (findings F-03): service-type cases now ALSO auto-apply via deterministic subject-matter match on the bid's cached tender title/description (patterns in trigger_condition, fixture data) - a security-services tender demands PSIRA registration regardless of buyer (VCW403/SECURE/25 listed valid company AND per-individual Grade B PSIRA registrations among its immediate-disqualification pre-qualifiers). For other sector registrations the pack demands, add the rule manually.
evidence_required: Certified, unexpired sector registration certificates matching the demanded class/grade

name: GATE-INSURANCE
title: Professional Indemnity / Public Liability at stated cover
trigger_condition: {"any_of": [{"institution_matches": ["cape town", "airports company", "acsa", "national roads agency", "sanral", "transnet", "tnpa", "passenger rail", "prasa", "air traffic and navigation", "atns", "vaal central water"]}, {"subject_matches": ["security service", "security solution", "guarding", "psira"]}]}
checklist_text: Insurance at the stated cover level: certificate or broker's letter of intent in the bid where demanded; note post-award insure-within-14-days regimes (failure can mean repudiation plus a 12-month bar)
guidance: Buyer-specific in amount and stage. v3: auto-applies via deterministic buyer match for buyers whose 2026-08 quirk sheets show standing insurance demands (per-buyer cover facts ship as data in params.buyer_cover_facts); for any other buyer add it when the pack demands insurance evidence. Note post-award insure-within-14-days regimes: at SANRAL, failure to deliver the insurance pack in time is the one post-award miss that converts into an automatic >=12-month bar from all its tenders. Wave-1 (findings F-03): Vaal Central Water added to the buyer list (VCW403/SECURE/25 made Public Liability Insurance of minimum R15 million an immediate-disqualification PRE-QUALIFIER - treat as Fatal on VCW packs despite this rule's Curable default), and security-services subject matching added - guarding packs routinely demand stated public-liability cover.
evidence_required: PI/PL certificate or broker letter at the stated cover
params: {"buyer_cover_facts": [{"match": "vaal central water", "detail": "Public Liability Insurance of minimum R15 million - listed among VCW403/SECURE/25's immediate-disqualification PRE-QUALIFIERS at bid stage; treat as Fatal on VCW packs"}, {"match": "cape town", "detail": "Public liability >= R20m per single claim in the supplier's name covering supplier and purchaser, plus motor vehicle liability and COIDA letter, evidenced via the prescribed Insurance Broker's Warranty pro-forma"}, {"match": "sanral", "detail": "PI, general public liability and third-party liability at R7.2m EACH, due within 14 calendar days of the Form of Acceptance with monthly proof thereafter; missing it triggers automatic >=12-month debarment from all future SANRAL tenders"}, {"match": "acsa", "detail": "Contract will not be signed without valid insurance and a COIDA letter of good standing; PI R5m held 24 months post-completion / PL R10m on professional services; airside construction largely covered by ACSA's Principal Controlled Insurance with contractor-borne deductibles (R75k-R250k)"}, {"match": "transnet", "detail": "NEC3 insurance tables in every construction/term-service RFP (motor vehicle liability minimum R5m indemnity); PI for design work at an employer-set limit; insurance costs deemed included in rates"}, {"match": "prasa", "detail": "Category-driven: PI + works insurance flagged for services, public-liability + contractor insurance on works categories, none on some supply-only panels; no Rand minimums stated in-pack"}, {"match": "air traffic and navigation", "detail": "'Adequate professional indemnity insurance' required generically; amounts deferred to the (unpopulated) SCC"}, {"match": "ethekwini", "detail": "Works packs: liability insurance R10m + SASRIA coupon policy in joint names (pack-specific, regime-covered rather than buyer-triggered)"}]}

name: GATE-MBD5
title: MBD 5 + three years' audited AFS (municipal above R10m)
checklist_text: MBD 5 declaration completed plus THREE years of audited annual financial statements (or AFS since incorporation if younger), with municipal-debt and prior-contract-performance disclosures
guidance: Municipal packs above R10 million demand this. If your AFS are not audited, resolve it months ahead - it cannot be fixed in a bid window.
evidence_required: MBD 5 + 3 years audited AFS

name: GATE-BANK-LETTER
title: Bank rating letter within its freshness window
checklist_text: Bank rating letter within the pack's freshness window (as tight as 1 month, stamped) - or bank statements / credit approval where the buyer rejects rating letters; read the evidence spec
guidance: Several buyers score or gate on a bank letter with all-or-nothing bands. v3: auto-applies via deterministic buyer match where the 2026-08 buyer sheets attest a standing demand - ACSA lists 'B4: Bank Letter: Letter of Good Standing from Bidder's Bank preferably with bank rating for tender sum' (evaluation-purposes returnable) plus a Letter of Solvency from the bidder's auditors/accountants. Eastern Cape Health services RFPs accept a rating letter OR financial statements as proof of financial resources (bid may be considered invalid without it). Not observed at the other profiled buyers - add manually when the pack scores financial standing.
evidence_required: Bank rating letter (stamped, within freshness window) or the pack's named alternative

name: GATE-SECURITY-VETTING
title: Post-scoring security / integrity vetting (security-adjacent buyers)
trigger_condition: {"institution_matches": ["sanral", "national roads agency", "transnet", "tnpa", "prasa", "passenger rail", "special investigating unit", "development bank of southern africa", "south african police", "border management", "home affairs", "airports company", "acsa"]}
checklist_text: Security-adjacent buyer flagged at go/no-go: post-scoring security/integrity vetting can override a winning score 'irrespective of the points scored' - SSA vetting, security clearances for staff AND subcontractors, original fingerprints for National Key Point work, SA-citizen-only personnel clauses; confirm the team can pass BEFORE committing bid costs
guidance: Corpus-wide mechanism the v1 guide missed: SIU Internal Integrity Unit + SSA vetting irrespective of points, SANRAL SSA screening, Transnet CONFIDENTIAL/SECRET/TOP SECRET clearances for staff and subcontractors, SAPS SAP-91 original fingerprints for National Key Point work, SA-citizen-only personnel clauses. Vetting failures override a winning score. v3 buyer-sheet facts: SANRAL makes State Security Agency screening a condition precedent to appointment and requires contractor-run pre-employment screening plus ANNUAL POLYGRAPH testing of deployed staff for the life of security contracts; Transnet's clearance clause appears even in low-value RFQs, covers subcontractors, and is at the bidder's own cost; PRASA demands a sworn Security Screening Form (bank details, director IDs, criminal-record declaration) WITH the bid on some KZN RFPs; ACSA reserves 'Security Vetting - if deemed necessary' at evaluation and vets airside access (induction training, permits) on every airport-site contract. Auto-applies via deterministic buyer match on the bid's institution (patterns are fixture data); for other packs naming vetting or clearances, add the rule manually.
evidence_required: Vetting/clearance readiness confirmed for every named person (and subcontractor) before go/no-go

name: KILL-01
title: Late submission - zero tolerance, measured in seconds
checklist_text: Delivery/upload scheduled at least 24 hours before closing; bid physically in the box / portal status 'complete' at closing - proof of posting or courier dispatch is NOT proof of delivery
guidance: The number-one bid killer, universal across the corpus: 'tenders arriving only a second after 12:00 or any time thereafter will not be accepted under any circumstance'. One buyer (DBSA) reserves sole discretion to accept a late bid where the lateness was the buyer's own fault, box access was denied, or a major incident occurred - never plan on it.
evidence_required: Lodgement receipt / portal confirmation

name: KILL-02
title: Missing / incomplete / unsigned mandatory returnables
checklist_text: Every returnable from the page-by-page master checklist present, completed and signed - and the pack's OWN checklist completed too, where it contains one
guidance: Universal in effect. Build a page-by-page master checklist of returnables on day one and have a second person independently re-verify every line before sealing.
evidence_required: Completed master checklist, second-person verification

name: KILL-03
title: Defaulters / restricted-suppliers listing
checklist_text: Defaulters check re-run close to submission: bidder or any director on the Register for Tender Defaulters / List of Restricted Suppliers is an automatic, no-cure disqualification
guidance: See GATE-DEFAULTERS; repeated here because the check must be re-run per bid, not assumed from the standing file.
evidence_required: Dated screenshot / extract of the Treasury list check

name: KILL-04
title: Fraudulent preference-points claim
checklist_text: Preference-point claims verified against CIPC/CSD/B-BBEE records - never inflate a claim: fraudulent claims carry disqualification, contract cancellation, up to 10-year restriction and criminal referral
guidance: Ownership percentages, names and addresses must match across CIPC, CSD, the B-BBEE evidence and the claim form; one buyer zeroes points outright where CIPC data and the affidavit disagree.
evidence_required: Cross-checked claim form vs CIPC/CSD/B-BBEE records

name: KILL-05
title: False or incomplete SBD/MBD 4 disclosure
checklist_text: SBD/MBD 4: every question answered individually (a blank is a kill); all directors listed with ID/tax numbers; ALL CSD-registered companies linked to any director disclosed - even ones unrelated to this bid
guidance: 'The accompanying bid will be disqualified if this disclosure is found not to be true and complete in every respect' - verbatim in 10+ packs. Understatement risks blacklisting, not just this bid.
evidence_required: Completed, signed SBD/MBD 4 per entity (per JV partner)

name: KILL-06
title: Collusion / attempts to influence
checklist_text: Independent bid determination certified (SBD/MBD 9 or the SBD 4 equivalent); communication ONLY with the designated contact - approaching other officials or councillors is itself a disqualifying offence at several buyers
guidance: Includes an untrue SBD/MBD 9. Universal in effect.
evidence_required: Signed SBD/MBD 9 (or SBD 4 anti-collusion section)

name: KILL-07
title: Uninitialled corrections, Tipp-Ex, pencil, wrong ink
checklist_text: Black non-erasable ink only; NO correction fluid anywhere; every correction single-line-through, rewritten and initialled by ALL signatories; every page initialled where required
guidance: A per-se disqualifier at many buyers - recurring but not 'half': the corpus black-ink mention rate is 17.5%, while other buyers run graduated consequence regimes, so check the pack's correction rule. One metro disqualifies for Tippex on the price schedule specifically: Tshwane names tippex/correction fluid on the price schedule as an automatic disqualifier and requires forms completed BY HAND in black pen (not re-typed or scanned) even though submission is e-portal-only. Mogale City goes further: handwritten-only, black-ink-only MBD forms, no electronic signatures, and pencil or any erasable pen invalidates the bid.
evidence_required: Document-integrity pass before sealing

name: KILL-08
title: Submission by fax / email / wrong channel
checklist_text: Only the prescribed channel used: physical buyers void fax/email submissions, portal buyers void everything off-platform; portal profile registered in the bidding entity's OWN name well in advance
guidance: Municipal is usually a physical box, SOE/national usually a portal, small RFQ often email - but verify per pack: a rare buyer accepts faxed and emailed tenders (SIU), so channel rules are per-pack even here, and packs can contradict themselves on the channel itself (advert says portal-only while boilerplate still describes a bid box) - add the submission channel to the day-one contradiction sweep. Bidding through another company's portal profile is banned at some SOEs. v3 buyer-sheet portal traps: Eskom is e-tendering-only (500MB/file, 4GB total, NO zip files, only the LATEST upload counts and status must show 'complete'); Transnet is eSupplier-portal-only (30MB/file, own-profile-only - submitting through another company's profile disqualifies even for a subsidiary - and only the ELECTRONIC price counts, the paper schedule is a decoy); Tshwane runs its e-portal with the tender box explicitly disabled; ACSA email-only packs demand the bid SPLIT into 4+ attachments of <=4MB each with no Cc/Bcc to any employee; Stats SA RFQs are email-only while its SBD1 header still advertises a bid box; ECDoH is eTenders-portal-only despite dead sealed-envelope boilerplate. Document fees run R300-R2,300+ at physical-issue buyers.
evidence_required: Channel confirmed from the pack's submission clause

name: KILL-09
title: Incomplete pricing schedule - blanks, dashes, unpriced lines
checklist_text: Every line priced including rate-only items - no blanks, dashes or N/A ('items against which N/A, left blank or - (dash) is entered... will also invalidate the tender'); write R0.00 deliberately; honour explicit NO QUOTE blocks; arithmetic recomputed; total reconciled to the cover form and Form of Offer in words AND figures
guidance: About half of packs make unpriced lines an explicit kill; a missing or mismatched carry-over to the cover form eliminates bids outright.
evidence_required: Priced schedule + arithmetic self-audit + reconciliation

name: KILL-10
title: Unsigned Form of Offer / no proof of signing authority
checklist_text: Form of Offer / cover form signed in original ink with capacity stated and witnessed where required; board resolution proving signing authority attached (signed by ALL directors where required)
guidance: 'Failure to submit proof of signing authority renders the tender non-responsive.' Fatal, not curable.
evidence_required: Signed offer + board/members' resolution + certified signatory ID

name: KILL-11
title: Functionality score below threshold
checklist_text: Realistic functionality self-score at or above the pack's threshold, criterion by criterion including sub-thresholds AND zero-anywhere rules (some buyers disqualify for a zero on ANY criterion even after the overall threshold is met); matched evidence sets attached per claimed project; every criterion cross-referenced to an exact page - 'not cross-referenced = not submitted'
guidance: Where functionality is scored, it is an elimination gate BEFORE price and preference: a cheap, B-BBEE-strong bid below the threshold is dead. But a sizeable minority of full formal bids run no functionality stage at all ('FUNCTIONALITY will not be used') - check the Tender Data's functionality clause, never infer it from pack size or sector. Claims without the prescribed documentary evidence score ZERO. Some buyers disqualify for a zero on ANY criterion or sub-criterion even after the overall threshold is met, and some per-criterion minimums equal the criterion maximum. Record the pack's threshold on the bid (functionality_threshold) and your self-score (functionality_self_score) - the submission gate compares them.
evidence_required: Self-score worksheet + evidence library cross-reference index

name: KILL-12
title: Qualified bid / own conditions attached
checklist_text: No conditions, qualifications or currency provisos attached to the offer or the price - treat 'never qualify' as the default: a qualified bid is non-responsive
guidance: 'Reject a non-responsive tender offer, and not allow it to be subsequently made responsive by correction or withdrawal of the non-conforming deviation.' A rare pack expressly permits qualifying the bid where an alteration is necessary (DWS boilerplate) - but treat 'never qualify' as the default.
evidence_required: Offer reviewed for stray conditions before sealing

name: KILL-13
title: Retyped or photocopied forms instead of the official ones
checklist_text: Official issued forms only - nothing retyped, redrafted or substituted; no pages removed or inserted; issued order preserved; inapplicable sections marked N/A rather than removed
guidance: 'ALL BIDS MUST BE SUBMITTED ON THE OFFICIAL FORMS PROVIDED - NOT TO BE RE-TYPED' - an explicit kill in about a third of packs.
evidence_required: Form-integrity pass before sealing

name: KILL-14
title: Missed clarification / cure window
checklist_text: Post-submission watch in place: the named contact email monitored DAILY for clarification/cure requests (windows run 24 hours to 7 days and are enforced literally); validity-extension requests answered in writing before expiry - and CHECK WHICH WAY the silence-default runs: silence can bind you to a stale price instead of excluding you
guidance: Even where a cure window exists it is 'the second chance you can still blow' - missing a 48-hour clarification deadline converts a curable defect into disqualification. Never assume a cure window exists: smaller municipal and provincial buyers are single-shot. On validity extensions the silence-default runs BOTH ways: at most buyers silence = exclusion, at Limpopo DoH silence = acceptance of the extension, and eThekwini's SCM policy auto-extends validity 12 months unless the bidder objects in writing. Agreeing to extend can also bar any modification of your tender (Eskom). v3: per-buyer cure regimes from the 2026-08 buyer sheets ship as data in params.cure_regimes (Eskom's four-tier ladder, Transnet's three-tier document classes, ATNS/Tshwane/ECDoH 7-day administrative windows, Mogale/Tourism single-shot). Stats SA can void a quote for missing a follow-up deadline that is never pre-published - treat any buyer email as same-day urgent.
evidence_required: Named contact + monitoring routine documented
params: {"cure_regimes": [{"match": "eskom", "detail": "Four tiers: disqualify-at-closing (pricing schedule) / 5-working-day cure on written request (most annexures) / score-zero-only (B-BBEE evidence) / pre-award-gate (CSD, tax, contractual requirements); CIDB grading proof runs its own separate deadline outside the 5-day cure"}, {"match": "transnet", "detail": "Three tiers: Mandatory (no cure) / Scoring (automatic zero) / Essential (one buyer-set resubmission window); non-material contractual deviations may be withdrawn on request before disqualification"}, {"match": "air traffic and navigation", "detail": "Stage-1 administrative gaps curable within 7 days (non-substantive only, at ATNS discretion); Stage-2 mandatory defects fatal; a single uncertified certificate is discarded and zero-scored with no cure"}, {"match": "tshwane", "detail": "7-day cure on request for CSD proof / RD.C document series and tax status only; every other returnable fatal on first miss"}, {"match": "prasa", "detail": "Bidders already found responsive get a buyer-set resubmission window for incomplete returnables; Stage-1 mandatory items, signatures, BOQ completeness and briefing non-attendance are fatal with no cure"}, {"match": "sanral", "detail": "Cure is exceptional and enumerated: 7 days to adjust flagged unbalanced rates; post-award 7 working days (SARS status) / 14 days (banking; insurance - and an insurance miss converts to an automatic >=12-month debarment)"}, {"match": "eastern cape", "detail": "ECDoH: 7-day cure for administrative-in-nature information and tax status on services RFPs; material deviations fatal and cannot be made responsive (SANS 10845)"}, {"match": "mogale", "detail": "Single-shot: 'instantly disqualified' mandatory tier and no-award essential tier, no condonation language anywhere in the sampled packs"}, {"match": "department of tourism", "detail": "Single-shot: disqualification-first drafting, no cure window or grace observed; buyer applies its own pricing-precedence rules instead of asking the bidder to fix"}, {"match": "statistics south africa", "detail": "Follow-up information requests carry buyer-communicated (not pre-published) deadlines - failure to meet them can render the quote non-responsive"}]}

name: KILL-15
title: Missed or arrived late at compulsory briefing
checklist_text: Compulsory briefing / site visit attended and ON TIME (15+ minutes early - lateness counts as absence); register signed in the exact name of the bidding entity; Certificate of Attendance filed into the bid
guidance: Where a briefing is compulsory, attendance is a pass/fail gate in every single case. Some buyers evaluate only entities on the register and issue addenda only to them. v3: headers and body can conflict on the compulsory status - clarify in writing; some buyers publish a doors-close grace period, but Transnet starts punctually and will NOT repeat information for late arrivals; SANRAL runs briefings virtually (Teams) with a 15-minute late-exclusion and a one-representative-per-tenderer rule; ECDoH holds no briefing at all on routine works packs yet makes attendance fatal (name on the official virtual attendance list) when one is held - never infer the regime from the buyer's habit.
evidence_required: Signed attendance register + Certificate of Attendance

name: KILL-16
title: Wrong tender box / unsealed or mislabelled envelope
checklist_text: Envelope sealed and endorsed exactly as prescribed (bid number, description, closing date, bidder name/address); one bid per envelope; correct copy count and ORIGINAL/COPY packages where required; courier instructed to put the bid IN THE BOX, not at reception
guidance: Defective labelling is itself a rejection ground; one buyer disqualifies for a single missing copy.
evidence_required: Packaging checked against the pack's endorsement spec

name: KILL-17
title: Page removal or document tampering
checklist_text: Complete document returned - no pages removed, no unbinding, no inserted pages, no 'dismembering'
guidance: Return the complete issued document; mark inapplicable sections N/A rather than removing them.
evidence_required: Page-count check against the issued pack

name: KILL-18
title: CSD inactive at closing
checklist_text: CSD status re-verified ACTIVE in the final week before closing (not just when the standing file was built)
guidance: Several buyers disqualify at evaluation if the CSD registration is not active at closing time - a stale standing file does not protect you.
evidence_required: Fresh CSD report inside the buyer's freshness window

name: KILL-19
title: Municipal rates in arrears (municipal buyers)
checklist_text: No municipal account (company or any director) in arrears beyond THIS buyer's threshold without a settlement arrangement - the threshold is buyer-specific: 90 days at some, ONE month at others (including arrears with any other municipality)
guidance: The enforcement side of GATE-RATES: arrears at evaluation is automatic disqualification at municipal buyers. The arrears threshold is not a flat 3 months - it runs 1-3 months by buyer (Kouga: one month, including any other municipality's arrears; eThekwini: no window at all - an Acknowledgement of Debt must exist at closing). Per-buyer windows ship as data on GATE-RATES params.arrears_windows.
evidence_required: Current rates statements / settlement arrangement

name: KILL-20
title: Pricing leaking into the technical envelope (two-envelope systems)
checklist_text: Where the pack runs a two-envelope system: technical volume swept for ANY price figure - including in CVs, org charts and past-project descriptions - before sealing
guidance: Any price figure appearing in the technical envelope is an explicit disqualification trigger at two-envelope buyers. Other buyers explicitly do NOT run two envelopes - never assume either way.
evidence_required: Documented sweep of the technical volume

name: KILL-21
title: JV defects - no signed (or notarised) JV agreement before submission
checklist_text: JV: signed JV agreement (not a letter of intent) before submission - notarised/authenticated formation document plus all-partner power of attorney where the pack demands it; per-partner CSD/TCS/SBD4; lead-partner grading rule met
guidance: A letter of intent to formalise later is expressly rejected; at some buyers a signed-but-unnotarised agreement fails eligibility.
evidence_required: Signed/notarised JV agreement + per-partner compliance pack

name: KILL-22
title: Missing addenda acknowledgements
checklist_text: Record of Addenda signed with a copy of every addendum attached; BoQ/pricing updated where an addendum changed it
guidance: Verbal answers at briefings are not binding - get every material clarification confirmed as a written addendum, then acknowledge every addendum in the bid. v3: read the clarification/question cut-off clause every time - CIDB packs run 3-5 working days (not 'typically five'), the Tender Data frequently overrides the CIDB default, question and addenda cut-offs can differ, and some windows anchor to the briefing date, not closing. Cape Town only guarantees addenda delivery to bidders who obtained the pack through its official Tender Distribution Office - out-of-channel downloads forfeit addendum notices.
evidence_required: Signed Record of Addenda + addendum copies

name: KILL-23
title: Unsanctioned alternative offers
checklist_text: No alternative price basis or alternative offer - including fixed rates in lieu of a prescribed CPA/escalation formula - unless the pack expressly permits alternatives, and then only alongside a fully compliant base offer
guidance: Distinct from a qualified bid: several buyers ban alternatives outright; one allows them only with prior permission AND a compliant base offer submitted alongside.
evidence_required: Offer basis checked against the pack's alternatives clause

name: KILL-24
title: Multiple bids / related-bidder conflicts - one bid per entity
checklist_text: ONE bid per entity: no second submission solo or via a JV (more than one bid voids ALL your submissions); related-company exposure checked before two group companies bid the same tender - JVs sharing directors/shareholders with another bidder are ineligible
guidance: Submitting more than one bid (solo or via JV) voids all your submissions, and JVs sharing directors or shareholders with another bidder are ineligible (eThekwini, SANRAL, Eskom). Some buyers add cooling-off bans for ex-employees/board members (SABC: 12 months; 5 years if dismissed).
evidence_required: Group/JV conflict check documented before submission

name: KILL-25
title: Dual-channel defects - which copy governs
checklist_text: Where the pack demands BOTH a hard copy and an electronic copy: check which regime the pack states - identical-or-invalid at some buyers, versus hard-copy-governs at others (eThekwini/ERWAT: the hard copy is the governing/ruling version, and at eThekwini the bid is INVALID without the hard copy even if uploaded)
guidance: Dual-channel buyers split two ways: identical-or-invalid at some, a precedence rule at others - eThekwini and ERWAT declare the hard copy the governing version if the two differ, and at eThekwini a bid without the hard copy is invalid even if uploaded. v3: ACSA's dual-channel packs are explicit that BOTH methods must be used, the physical submission takes precedence on any discrepancy, and missing the physical drop before closing is a disqualification even if the email arrived complete and on time (hard-copy-governs buyers ship as data in params). Contrast: SANRAL bundles the memory-stick electronic copy INSIDE the one sealed envelope (a single channel, not dual), and PRASA accepts content from any submitted format with no stated hierarchy. Never assume either regime; read the pack's submission clause.
evidence_required: Both copies lodged per the pack's dual-channel clause; governing-copy rule noted
params: {"hard_copy_governs_patterns": ["ethekwini", "erwat", "airports company", "acsa"], "wet_ink_hard_copy_patterns": ["ethekwini", "free state department of public works", "fs public works"]}

name: SCORE-SYSTEM
title: 80/20 vs 90/10 preference system threshold (R50m, all taxes included)
guidance: 80/20 for tender value up to and including R50 million (all applicable taxes included), 90/10 above it - confirmed from the TENDER-SPECIFIC clause, never the boilerplate. Some buyers determine the system only AFTER tenders are received; a price that could straddle R50m must carry a points strategy that works under both systems (the computed preference_system field shows 'Straddling' inside the configured band). Updating the threshold or band is a fixture/desk edit, no code changes.

name: SCORE-PRICE-FORMULA
title: Price-to-points formula Ps = X * (1 - (Pt - Pmin)/Pmin)
guidance: Lowest responsive price takes all 80 (or 90) points; everyone else scores on Ps = X * (1 - (Pt - Pmin)/Pmin) with X per the applicable system. Proximity to the lowest acceptable price dominates; preference points decide among close prices. For disposal/leasing/income-generating tenders the formula INVERTS - the highest acceptable offer scores full points: Ps = X * (1 + (Pt - Pmax)/Pmax). Best-and-final-offer negotiation rounds mean the submitted price is not always the evaluated price, and award cascades to the next-ranked bidder on decline or delivery default at several buyers - 2nd place stays live past award. Computed deterministically by tender.compliance.scoring.price_points() / price_points_inverted().

name: SCORE-FUNCTIONALITY
title: Functionality threshold - elimination gate before price/preference
guidance: The threshold is per-tender data, never a constant: read from the pack by a human and stored per bid (functionality_threshold). v3 corpus scan (2026-08, ~1,200 packs): an explicit minimum threshold appears in 238 documents; mode AND median are 70 (70 alone is 52.5% of observations, and the market clusters on [70, 80]); observed range 36-100. 60 is common for catering/work-study/general services and 80 for leases, financial services and high-risk technical packs; low-tail values (36/40/50) are mostly RAW POINT scores on non-100 scales (e.g. 36 out of 65 ~ 55%), not percentages - a sub-60 bar is not a typo, but check the scale. Use 70% only as the planning default when a pack is silent or ambiguous - the submission gate still compares functionality_self_score to the recorded per-tender threshold, and stats never override pack data. The pipeline is usually compliance (pass/fail) then functionality vs threshold, then price and preference for survivors only - but a sizeable minority of full formal bids run no functionality stage at all, and some RFPs score price first with a pass/fail risk review after: check the Tender Data's functionality clause. Some buyers disqualify for a zero on ANY criterion even above the overall threshold, and some add live-demo stages with 100% component thresholds (ATNS). Buyer norms from the 2026-08 sheets: Eskom 80; PRASA 70-80 by category; Dept of Tourism 80; Transnet construction RFPs 60; ACSA 60-75 by complexity; ECDoH bimodal (none on routine works, 70+ on specialised/services); Mogale panel entry as low as ~55%.

name: SCORE-TIEBREAK
title: Tie-break cascade: preference points, then functionality, then lots
guidance: Where total points are equal, several packs award to the bidder with the higher specific-goals/preference points, then the higher functionality score, and only then a draw of lots - so maximising claimable goals and functionality margin matters even when expecting to win on price.

name: SCORE-OBJECTIVE-CRITERIA
title: PPPFA s2(1)(f) objective-criteria override - winning on points is necessary, not sufficient
guidance: Many buyers (Transnet, Eskom, SANRAL, DBSA, CSIR, PPECB, Johannesburg Water and others) reserve a named post-scoring stage under PPPFA s2(1)(f) that can pass over the top-ranked bidder: poor track record with that buyer, litigation against the buyer, supplier rotation, financial-ratio risk analysis, insolvency/business rescue, director fraud charges, or lookback windows (18 months post-termination at DBSA). Winning on points is necessary, not sufficient. Related post-scoring security/integrity vetting is covered by GATE-SECURITY-VETTING. Flag exposure (prior disputes, litigation, financial ratios) at go/no-go - this stage cannot be computed from bid data, so the record ships as guidance.

name: SCORE-PANEL
title: Panel / framework two-stage mechanics - entry buys the right to compete, not revenue
guidance: Panel/framework tenders run their own two-stage mechanics, recurring across municipal and SOE packs: a functionality-only gate to join the panel (sometimes no price submitted at panel stage at all), then per-order RFQ mini-competitions at 80/20 among panelists, cascades to the next-ranked panelist on decline, ongoing performance-penalty/greylisting regimes, one-area/lot caps, leased-equipment cross-checks against other bidders' fleets, and exclusion for repeatedly ignoring RFQ invitations. Estimated quantities are NOT guaranteed volume - price each unit to be viable at any volume, and factor the panel-stage bid cost into go/no-go.

name: GATE-POPIA
title: POPIA consent / personal-information returnable
trigger_condition: {"any_of": [{"institution_matches": ["sanral", "national roads agency", "transnet", "tnpa"]}, {"subject_matches": ["popia", "protection of personal information", "personal information", "website", "web site", "hosting", "helpdesk", "help desk", "ticketing", "call centre", "call center", "customer service system", "customer relationship management"]}]}
checklist_text: POPIA compliance surface confirmed for THIS pack: consent/processing form completed, signed and returned where the pack demands one (SANRAL Form A13; Transnet's standalone returnable section; a mandatory 'Consent (POPIA)' line item at some provincial buyers), AND - on tenders whose subject is processing personal information (website/hosting, helpdesk/ticketing, call-centre systems) - the pack's POPIA/PAIA specification demands identified and evidenced (data-residency/SA-hosting clauses, retention periods for recorded citizen data, breach/security obligations)
guidance: A POPIA consent/processing form is a mandatory returnable at multiple buyers across construction, municipal and SOE packs (rules-table GATE-POPIA). v3 buyer-sheet facts: SANRAL ships it as a standing returnable form (A13); Transnet as a standalone returnable section in both RFQ and RFP packs; Eastern Cape Health lists 'Protection of personal information: Consent (POPIA)' as a mandatory line item and annexes a full department-drafted POPIA agreement. At other profiled buyers POPIA appears as a contractual clause rather than a returnable - no form to file there, but read what you are consenting to. Wave-1 (findings F-03): the rule now ALSO auto-applies via deterministic subject-matter match on the bid's cached tender title/description - a tender whose subject IS processing personal information carries POPIA obligations regardless of buyer: Musina 18-2025/26 (cloud helpdesk/ticketing) demands 'compliance with POPIA, PAIA, and related legislations' as explicit specification text (section 4(c)), SA-only hosting and 18-month retention of recorded citizen calls; a municipal website-hosting tender (TWK COR 01/2026/27) processes residents' personal information end to end. Patterns are fixture data; desk-add elsewhere when the pack lists a POPIA returnable.
evidence_required: Signed POPIA consent/processing form on the pack's own template

name: GATE-INTEGRITY-PACT
title: Buyer-branded Integrity Pact + DPIP/FPPO declaration
checklist_text: Buyer-branded Integrity Pact signed and returned IN ADDITION to SBD/MBD 9 (Eskom: Supplier Integrity Pact + Annexure D Integrity Declaration; Transnet: Service Provider/Supplier Integrity Pact T2.2 schedule); the related DPIP/FPPO politically-exposed-persons and former-employee declarations completed where demanded - omission can render the tender invalid
guidance: A buyer-branded Integrity Pact must be signed and returned in addition to the standard SBD/MBD 9 anti-collusion certificate at Gauteng Treasury, Eskom and Transnet-style buyers (rules-table GATE-INTEGRITY-PACT). v3 buyer-sheet facts: Eskom's Annexure D Integrity Declaration doubles as a data-processing consent and disqualifies for procurement abuse or fraud; Transnet's Integrity Pact is a standard returnable schedule across NEC3 RFPs and RFQ packs, paired with a DPIP/FPPO disclosure (Transnet publishes its DPIP/FPPO contracts annually) and a 10-YEAR former-employee/board-member lookback whose incomplete disclosure 'will lead to the disqualification of a response'. SANRAL distributes the same function across its A5-A15 declaration forms (DPIP disclosure, fronting certificate) without an integrity-pact document by that name. Auto-applies via deterministic buyer match; desk-add for other packs that bundle a branded pact.
evidence_required: Signed buyer-branded Integrity Pact + DPIP/FPPO / former-employee declarations per the pack

name: GATE-LOCALITY
title: Locality: eligibility gate, scored points, or post-award levy
checklist_text: Locality treatment determined for THIS pack: a HARD eligibility gate (ATNS 'Locality Footprint' Stage-2 mandatory - proof of presence in the exact municipal/provincial area via municipality bill, lease, title deed, councillor letter or local-partner MOU; Dept of Tourism - office in the bid province, physically verified by site visit before award, one cluster/province per bidder), SCORED preference points (Mogale 5/3/2/0 municipal>district>province ladder; Tshwane 4/2/1; eThekwini/PRASA municipal-boundary points), or a post-award LEVY (Mogale City deducts 2% of every payment from non-local winners, with a signed acceptance declaration as a returnable) - prove it, price it, or self-eliminate accordingly
guidance: Locality can be a hard eligibility gate, a scored criterion, or a post-award levy (rules-table DELTA-V2-18) - three different consequences that demand different responses: evidence, points strategy, or margin. v3 buyer-sheet facts: ATNS makes 'Locality Footprint' a fatal Stage-2 mandatory requirement tied to its station-based operating model; Dept of Tourism disqualifies bidders whose claimed office fails a physical site visit and locks bidders to one cluster/province; Mogale City both scores a 5/3/2/0 geographic ladder AND levies 2% of every payment on non-local winners; eThekwini requires local presence within the municipal boundary for the contract duration on some packs, on top of ETM>KZN>SA locality points; PRASA scores municipal-boundary and rural-residency points (Induna/chief letters accepted as evidence); ECDoH scopes locality points to the issuing health DISTRICT - out-of-district bidders are told outright they cannot claim them. Auto-applies via deterministic buyer match where locality can gate or levy; for points-only buyers it is a scoring-strategy check.
evidence_required: Locality proof per the pack (municipal account/bill, lease, title deed, councillor/tribal letter, or local-partner agreement) - or the levy priced into the offer

name: SCORE-PREF-CLAIM
title: Preference points: written claim + exact named proof, or zero
checklist_text: Preference points claimed EXPLICITLY in writing per goal on SBD/MBD 6.1 (the NUMBER of points per goal - ticks are rejected at some buyers) with the exact named proof attached per goal: a claim without proof scores zero, proof without a written claim scores zero, and certification stamps older than the buyer's window (6 months at Stats SA RFQs) zero the goal too
guidance: Preference points must be explicitly claimed in writing per goal on SBD/MBD 6.1 with the exact named proof attached - a claim without proof scores zero, and proof without a written claim scores zero (rules-table SCORE-PREF-CLAIM). The goal BASKET is buyer- and even contract-type-specific (eThekwini swaps Race/locality baskets for Gender/local-content on goods packs; Cape Town and ECDoH run PPR-2022 specific-goals models where a B-BBEE certificate is only supporting evidence; Eskom has scored a graduate-placement goal), so read the buyer's own table before assuming the standard B-BBEE ladder. JV rules are strict: Dept of Tourism refuses JV affidavits and demands a consolidated agency-issued certificate regardless of member size; SANRAL wants a project-specific consolidated JV certificate bearing the contract name and number. Stats SA RFQs zero a goal when the Commissioner-of-Oaths stamp on any certified proof is older than 6 months. Points-only severity: an honest missed claim never kills the bid - but a FRAUDULENT claim does (KILL-04).
evidence_required: Completed SBD/MBD 6.1 with points written per goal + the pack's exact named proof per goal (certification stamps inside the buyer's window)

name: PRICE-VAT
title: VAT treatment: deemed-inclusive thresholds and silent defaults
checklist_text: VAT treatment confirmed from THIS pack before pricing: several buyers DEEM prices above a threshold (R1m-R2.3m by buyer) VAT-INCLUSIVE regardless of what was written - an exclusive-priced bidder absorbs the full 15%; non-vendors pushed past R1m turnover must price VAT in and register with SARS within ~21 days of award; simple RFQs often default VAT-EXCLUSIVE if silent - never assume either way
guidance: Several buyers deem prices above a threshold (R1m-R2.3m) VAT-inclusive regardless of what was written, so an exclusive-priced bidder silently absorbs the 15%; non-vendors whose award pushes them past R1m turnover must price VAT in and register with SARS within ~21 days of award; simple RFQs often default VAT-EXCLUSIVE when silent (rules-table DELTA-V2-17). At some buyers wrong VAT treatment is an outright kill, not a margin loss: DWS's VOCMA packs state 'Bidders who are registered for VAT who submit bids without VAT will be disqualified'. Severity Curable reflects the general case (a pricing trap); treat it as fatal wherever the pack names it a disqualifier.
evidence_required: Pack's VAT clause read; price built on the confirmed basis (and SARS vendor status checked against the award value)

name: PRICE-SECURITY
title: Performance security, retention and post-award financial deliverables - priced in
checklist_text: Performance security, retention and post-award financial deliverables PRICED before bidding: security runs 5-20% of contract value (or a flat Rand sum) due within 14-30 days of award, retention/payment-reduction regimes commonly replace it under ~R1m, and some buyers convert a missed post-award financial deliverable into automatic debarment - also check for most-favoured-customer clauses, no-arithmetic-correction rules (submitted total final), price-declaration forms that GOVERN over the schedule, and withdrawal-after-acceptance liability equal to the re-procurement price gap
guidance: Performance security is 5-10% OR a flat Rand sum within 14-21 days in the corpus baseline, often replaced by a ~5% payment-reduction retention under ~R1m (rules-table DELTA-V2-23) - and the buyer sheets widen the range: ACSA takes an unconditional on-demand bond of 20% of the Prices plus 5% retention; eThekwini scales it (nil <=R1m, 5% to R10m, 10% above, with 10% retention capped at 5% and no interest paid); SANRAL 5% of the design portion within 14 days; Eskom reserves a discretionary 10% bond for bidders whose financial standing is weak (nominate two Eskom-approved institutions); DWS expressly WAIVES it for plant-hire/materials packs; the GCC default defers the figure to the SCC within 30 days of award. Also from DELTA-V2-23: most-favoured-customer clauses, no-arithmetic-correction buyers (the submitted total is final), price-declaration forms governing over the schedule (SANRAL: the Pricing Schedule governs over the Form of Offer total), and withdrawal-after-acceptance liability equal to the re-procurement price gap. None of this blocks submission - it decides whether the price survives the contract.
evidence_required: Security/retention regime extracted from the pack and priced into the offer; guarantee facility confirmed with the bank/insurer before award

name: FORM-VALIDITY
title: Bid validity recorded - mode 90 days, price the longer figure
checklist_text: Bid validity recorded from the pack (mode 90 days; 30-180 all common; outliers to 365 - and check CALENDAR vs BUSINESS days): where the pack asks the bidder to state a validity, or two different figures appear, price for the LONGER period and clarify in writing; diarise the expiry date - extension requests are then handled under the cure-watch rule (KILL-14)
guidance: Bid validity guidance widened in v2 from 60-120 days to mode 90 with 30-180 all common and outliers to 365, calendar or business days (rules-table DELTA-V2-11). Some packs ask the bidder to state a validity - if two figures appear, price the longer and clarify in writing. Buyer-sheet wrinkles: Transnet deems the SUCCESSFUL bidder's validity open-ended ('valid until a final contract has been concluded'), which can hold #2/#3 at their quoted price after losing; ATNS requires Tax and B-BBEE certificates to still be valid AT AWARD, beyond the general validity window; ACSA grants a CPI price-review right only if its own evaluation overruns the 12-week validity. Hold prices realistically for the recorded window - withdrawal after acceptance can cost the re-procurement price gap (PRICE-SECURITY).
evidence_required: Validity period (and day-type) recorded on the bid file; expiry diarised

name: WARN-PREF-CONFLICT
title: Conflicting preference frameworks in one pack - complete EVERY framework's form
checklist_text: Where the pack carries MORE THAN ONE preference framework (e.g. the operative PPR 2022 specific-goals SBD/MBD 6.1 table ALONGSIDE a pre-2011 HDI equity-ownership claim form and/or a Local Government Ordinance 1939 local-content/SABS certificate): identify which framework the evaluation clause actually scores, then complete and sign EVERY framework's form anyway - the legacy forms state that non-completion forfeits the preference
guidance: Wave-1 (findings F-12), grounded in the Musina 18-2025/26 helpdesk pack: it simultaneously carries (a) the operative PPR 2022 MBD 6.1 specific-goals table (80/20; HDI 10 / women 4 / disability 3 / youth 3), (b) the pre-2011 HDI equity-ownership framework (a full PPPFA 2000 Preference Point Explanation, NEP = NOP x EP/100, and buyer-authored Form C claiming 'points out of 20'), and (c) a Local Government Ordinance 1939 local-content/SABS preference certificate (Form D). Only one framework scores, but Form C and Form D each state that non-completion forfeits the preference. The deterministic lint in compliance/preference_frameworks.py (also wired into the pack builder's manifest warnings) detects the frameworks by normalized-substring signals over the pack's form names/kill notes and warns when more than one is present; the signal patterns ship as data in params.framework_patterns. No auto trigger: with per-pack returnable capture not yet in the SDK (findings F-02), attach this rule manually when triage finds a second framework in a pack.
evidence_required: Every preference-framework form in the pack completed and signed; the operative scoring framework noted on the bid file
params: {"framework_patterns": {"PPR 2022 specific goals (SBD/MBD 6.1)": ["ppr 2022", "preferential procurement regulations, 2022", "preferential procurement regulations 2022", "specific goals", "specific-goals"], "Pre-2011 HDI equity-ownership (PPPFA 2000 regulations)": ["hdi equity", "equity ownership", "nep = nop", "points out of 20", "preferential procurement regulations, 2001", "preferential procurement regulations 2001"], "Local Government Ordinance 1939 local content / SABS": ["ordinance, 1939", "ordinance 1939", "local government ordinance", "sabs mark"]}}
